text:
Predicates:
Costs(x, y) ::: It costs y dollars to take the x test.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provides(z, x, y) ::: z provides financial aid to those x applicants who prove economic hardship.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to take the y test.
Premises:
Costs(GRE, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
Provides(ETS, GRE, financial_aid) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
(SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x)) → ProveHardship(x) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
Applying(tom, GRE) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Costs(GRE, y) ∧ y < 300 ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
